title: Tenant-level throughput contracts and autoscale synthesizer
creator: Marco Chen
description: Goal: Build a tenant-aware throughput contract model and an autoscale synthesizer that recommends capacity changes and headroom budgets for Dedicated pools. Background: customers running Dedicated pools ask for predictable per-tenant throughput guarantees while minimizing cost. Current signals (pool-level utilization, p95 latency) are insufficient for tenant-level right-sizing. This ticket implements a pipeline to ingest tenant request traces, compute per-tenant steady-state throughput, model SLO headroom, simulate autoscale policies under realistic traffic, and surface action recommendations through a Console dashboard and an API. The outcome will be a repeatable recommendation flow that produces: 1) per-tenant recommended commit and burst allowances, 2) suggested autoscale policy parameters (scale step, cooldown, target utilization), and 3) expected cost delta and p95 latency impact estimates.
acceptance_criteria: Data pipeline ingests 30 days of tenant-level request/tokens and produces per-tenant throughput and peak-percentile curves
Simulation harness runs autoscale scenarios and outputs expected latency and cost metrics for at least 3 policy variants
Console dashboard displays per-tenant utilization heatmap, recommended commit (vCPU/GPU-equivalent) and suggested autoscale params
API endpoint available for programmatic recommendations (GET /v1/dedicated/recommendations?pool_id=&tenant_id=)
Recommendation accuracy validated against synthetic replay with <10% error on predicted cost and <5% error on predicted p95 latency for top-10 tenants
Documentation (design + runbook) published and reviewed by SRE and Product
tasks: Instrument tenant-level telemetry in serving runtime: tags for tenant_id, request_size, model_variant, and routing path
Build ETL to roll up tenant-hourly metrics and store compressed prefix/KV cache hit rates
Implement autoscale simulator that models queueing, batch formation, burst pools, and cooldown behavior
Design recommendation heuristics: commit suggestion, burst cap, target_utilization, scale_step, cooldown_s
Wire recommendations into Console: UI mockups -> front-end implementation -> backend API
Add unit/integration tests and run synthetic replays for validation
Write runbook for operator actions when recommendations conflict with SLA constraints

notes: Design tradeoffs: conservative recommendations (overprovisioning) reduce SLA breach risk but increase cost. We'll expose a risk slider in the Console to tune between 'conservative', 'balanced', and 'aggressive' modes.
Privacy: tenant identifiers in telemetry will be hashed for any analytics exported outside VPCs. Ensure KMS integration for keys used in anonymization.
Operational concern: automated apply requires strict RBAC and audit logging; coordinate with Security for approval before enabling auto-apply for customers with high compliance needs.
